# Nix & NixOS Enterprise Production & Internals — Comprehensive Syllabus

**Working title:** Mastering Nix & NixOS: From Store Mechanics to Production Architecture  
**Baseline release (as of 2026-07):** **NixOS / nixpkgs 26.05 “Yarara”** (stable channel; systemd stage-1 initrd default).  
**Prior baseline:** 25.11 “Xantusia”. **Upcoming target:** 26.11 “Zokor”.  

---

## 0. Executive Summary & Production Contract

### 0.1 Paradigm Shift
Traditional Linux administration (RHEL, Ubuntu, Debian, Arch) relies on imperative, mutable state mutations in global directories (`/usr/lib`, `/etc`, `/var`), resulting in snowflake servers, configuration drift, and non-reproducible deployments. 

Nix redefines package management and operating system configuration as **purely functional, lazy, mathematical evaluations**:
$$\text{Inputs (Nix Code + Source Archives)} \xrightarrow{\text{Evaluation}} \text{Derivations (.drv)} \xrightarrow{\text{Realization}} \text{Immutable Store Paths (/nix/store/<hash>-<name>)}$$

This syllabus serves as an expert-level, battle-tested blueprint for mastering Nix and NixOS from core store mechanics to production fleet orchestration, secret zero-trust injection, binary cache build farms, and evaluator internals.

### 0.2 Three-Tier Professional Competency Framework

| Tier | Informal Certification | Industry Equivalent | Scope & Target Outcomes |
|------|------------------------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| **Tier 1 — Foundation** | **NCA** (Nix Certified Associate) | RHCSA / LFCS | Fluent in store mechanics, Nix expression language, devShells, and single-host NixOS administration & recovery. |
| **Tier 2 — Professional** | **NCP** (Nix Certified Professional) | RHCE / CKA | Able to package polyglot software from source, author custom typed NixOS modules, manage dotfiles via Home Manager, structure Flakes workspaces, and encrypt secrets. |
| **Tier 3 — Expert & Architect** | **NCE** (Nix Certified Expert) | RHCA / Senior SRE | Capable of zero-touch remote provisioning (`nixos-anywhere` + `disko`), fleet deployment (Colmena / deploy-rs), operating private binary caches (Attic / Harmonia), running headless VM integration tests (`nixosTest`), security hardening, and evaluator profiling. |

---

### 0.3 Baseline 26.05 Landscape & 2026 Ecosystem Reality

- **Stage-1 Initrd Default:** NixOS 26.05 defaults to **systemd-based stage 1** (scripted stage 1 is deprecated). All storage, LUKS auto-unlock, and early boot recovery strategies in this syllabus reflect systemd initrd mechanics.
- **Implementations & Tooling Literacy:**
  - **Classic Nix:** Canonical C++ evaluator maintained by the NixOS Foundation.
  - **Determinate Nix:** Downstream distribution featuring parallel evaluation, Lazy Trees, and FlakeHub integration.
  - **Lix:** Community fork focused on C++ codebase modernization and stable flake features.
  - **Tvix:** Next-generation Rust-based modular evaluator (tracked for deep research).
- **Darwin Path:** 26.05 marks the final nixpkgs release supporting `x86_64-darwin`. Apple Silicon (`aarch64-darwin`) remains tier-1.

# Part 00 — Front Matter & Ecosystem Map

### Ch 00.1 — Syllabus & Production Contract (This Document)

### Ch 00.2 — How to Study & Lab Ground Rules
- **Lab Infrastructure:** Dedicated KVM/LXD VMs or disposable cloud instances (never run destructive experiments on daily-driver hosts).
- **Storage Budget:** Allocate $\ge 50\text{ GB}$ for `/nix/store` on lab hosts.
- **Generation Retention Policy:** Maintain minimum 5 system generations for safe rollback testing.

### Ch 00.3 — Mental Map of the Ecosystem
#### 00.3.1 The Architectural Triad
- **The Nix Language:** Pure, lazy, domain-specific functional programming language.
- **The Nix Package Manager & Store:** Input-addressed / content-addressed storage engine (`/nix/store`) and build sandbox.
- **NixOS:** Linux distribution built entirely on top of the Nix module system and systemd.

#### 00.3.2 Core Store Objects
- Evaluation Phase vs. Realization Phase.
- Derivations (`.drv` files), closures, profiles, and generation symlinks.

---

# Part 01 — First Steps: Store Architecture & Dual CLI Survival

### Ch 01.1 — Why Infrastructure Engineers Move to Nix
- **Root Cause Analysis:** Failure modes of imperative package managers (`apt`, `dnf`, `brew`) — dependency collisions, non-reproducible `/usr/lib` state, and un-auditable global mutations.
- **Hermetic Isolation:** Software builds modeled as side-effect-free mathematical functions of explicit inputs.

### Ch 01.2 — Installation Models & The Dual CLI Landscape
- **Daemon Architecture:** Multi-user daemon installation (`nix-daemon`) vs. single-user mode; socket activation and trust boundaries.
- **Installer Comparison:** Official Nix installer vs. Determinate installer (defaults, uninstall cleanliness, telemetry choices).
- **Dual CLI Mapping:**

| Legacy CLI | Modern Unified CLI (`flakes`) | Purpose |
|------------|--------------------------------|---------|
| `nix-env -iA` | `nix profile install` | User package management (prefer declarative devShells) |
| `nix-build` | `nix build` | Realize derivation outputs |
| `nix-shell` | `nix develop` / `nix shell` | Ephemeral interactive environments |
| `nix-channel` | flake inputs / lockfiles | Version locking and input tracking |
| `nix-collect-garbage` | `nix store gc` | Reclaim unreferenced store paths |

### Ch 01.3 — The Store Engine Without Magic
- **Store Path Hashing:** `/nix/store/<32-char-hash>-<name>-<version>`. How input-addressed hashes are calculated from derivation inputs.
- **Derivations (`.drv`):** Structure of `.drv` JSON/ATerm objects; environment variables, builders, and input closures.
- **Fixed-Output Derivations (FODs):** Fetching network sources safely by declaring content hashes (`sha256` / `sri`) upfront.
- **Profiles, Generations & GC Roots:**
  - GC root categories: `/nix/var/nix/gcroots`, symlinks in `/run/current-system`, and project result symlinks.
  - GC failure modes: why disk space isn't freed (hidden `.direnv` roots, result links, live user profiles).
  - Store hardlink optimization: `nix store optimise` / `auto-optimise-store = true`.

# Part 02 — Nix Language Mechanics, Laziness & `lib` Mastery

### Ch 02.1 — Language Fundamentals & Primitive Types
- Data types: `string`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `path`, `null`.
- Data structures: Lists (`[ 1 2 3 ]`), Attribute Sets (`{ a = 1; b = 2; }`).
- Strings and paths: Path literals vs. string coercion; multiline strings (`''...''`); string context (how strings carry store dependencies).

### Ch 02.2 — Functions, Scoping & FP Idioms
- Currying and single-argument function semantics (`x: y: x + y`).
- Attribute set pattern matching (`{ a, b, ... }@args:`), default values, and rest bindings.
- Scoping rules: `let ... in`, `inherit`, `rec` attrsets (and why `rec` is discouraged in large codebases due to evaluation recursion risks), `with` statements (and static analysis pitfalls).

### Ch 02.3 — Lazy Evaluation Dynamics & Debugging
- **Call-by-Need & Thunks:** How lazy evaluation defers computation until values are explicitly forced.
- **Infinite Data Structures:** Constructing lazy infinite lists/sets without stack overflow.
- **Debugging Toolkit:** `nix repl`, `builtins.trace`, `builtins.seq`, `builtins.deepSeq`, and reading distant evaluation stack traces.

### Ch 02.4 — `builtins` & `nixpkgs.lib` Deep Dive
- Essential `builtins`: `map`, `filter`, `foldl'`, `readDir`, `readFile`, `fromJSON`, `toJSON`, `attrNames`, `attrValues`.
- Standard library (`lib`):
  - Attrsets: `lib.mapAttrs`, `lib.filterAttrs`, `lib.recursiveUpdate`, `lib.attrByPath`.
  - Combinators & Logic: `lib.mkIf`, `lib.mkMerge`, `lib.mkDefault`, `lib.mkForce`, `lib.mkOverride`, `lib.mkOrder`.
  - Fixed Points: `lib.fix` and `lib.extends` (foundation for overlays and the module system).

# Part 03 — Nixpkgs User-Space: Pinning, Overrides & Polyglot DevShells

### Ch 03.1 — Package Discovery & Version Pinning
- Attribute paths vs. package names; search engines (`search.nixos.org`, `nix search`).
- Release channels: `nixos-26.05` vs. `nixpkgs-unstable`.
- Pinning methods: Flake inputs (`flake.lock`), `npins`, `niv`, and historical channel tracking.

### Ch 03.2 — Overriding & Patching Packages
- **`override`:** Modifying function arguments passed to `callPackage`.
- **`overrideAttrs`:** Modifying derivation attributes (`src`, `patches`, `postInstall`, `buildInputs`).
- Applying custom patches (`fetchpatch`) and version overrides without mutating upstream tree source.

### Ch 03.3 — Reproducible Project Shells (`devShells`)
- Authoring shells with `pkgs.mkShell` and `pkgs.mkShellNoCC`.
- `buildInputs` vs. `nativeBuildInputs` in development environments.
- Integration: `direnv` + `nix-direnv` for seamless environment loading.
- **Stateful Services in Dev Shells:** Running unprivileged local database instances (PostgreSQL, Redis, MySQL) inside project root directories using `shellHook` or `devenv` / `process-compose`.
- **FHS Environments:** `pkgs.buildFHSEnv` for executing non-nixified binaries (VS Code extensions, proprietary tools).

# Part 04 — Single Machine Administration & Recovery (NixOS 26.05)

### Ch 04.1 — Installation Architecture & Systemd Stage 1
- Disk partitioning: GPT, EFI System Partition (ESP), swap, Ext4/Btrfs layout.
- `nixos-generate-config` analysis: `configuration.nix` vs. `hardware-configuration.nix`.
- **Systemd Stage 1 (26.05 Baseline):** Understanding systemd initrd defaults, kernel modules loading, and target units in stage 1.

### Ch 04.2 — Configuration Anatomy & Rebuild Mechanics
- Evaluating system derivations; activation scripts and `/etc` managed symlink farm.
- Rebuild modes:

```text
nixos-rebuild switch       --> Build, activate now, set as default boot generation
nixos-rebuild boot         --> Build, set as default boot generation (activate on reboot)
nixos-rebuild test         --> Build, activate now (do NOT add to boot menu)
nixos-rebuild dry-activate --> Build, simulate systemd service activation steps
```

### Ch 04.3 — Networking, Users & Systemd Services
- Declarative user accounts (`users.users.<name>`), SSH authorized keys, and sudoer rules.
- Networking: `networking.hostName`, `systemd-networkd` vs. NetworkManager, `networking.firewall` (nftables).
- Systemd service encapsulation: `systemd.services.<name>` blocks, timers (`systemd.timers.<name>`), and journald log rotation.

### Ch 04.4 — Disaster Recovery & Generation Management
- Boot menu selection; rolling back safely from broken activation scripts or bad kernel modules.
- **Recovery Lab:** Deliberately corrupting networking/firewall settings, booting into prior generation, and conducting post-mortem analysis.

# Part 05 — Flakes Architecture, Locks & Repo Structuring

### Ch 05.1 — Flake Schema & Lock Discipline
- Structure of `flake.nix`: `description`, `inputs`, `outputs`.
- Lockfile (`flake.lock`) mechanics: cryptographic hash pinning, input deduplication via `follows`.
- Modern ecosystem stance: Flakes experimental flag vs. de-facto industry standard (Determinate Nix vs. Lix vs. Upstream).

### Ch 05.2 — Standard Flake Outputs Schema
- Per-system outputs: `packages.<system>`, `devShells.<system>`, `apps.<system>`, `checks.<system>`.
- System-agnostic outputs: `nixosConfigurations`, `homeConfigurations`, `overlays`, `nixosModules`, `templates`.
- Multi-system abstraction: using `flake-utils` or `flake-parts` to eliminate architecture boilerplate.

### Ch 05.3 — Migration Bridge: `configuration.nix` $\rightarrow$ Flakes
- Refactoring traditional `/etc/nixos/configuration.nix` into `nixosConfigurations.<hostname>`.
- Injecting custom inputs (`self`, `inputs`) into NixOS modules via `specialArgs`.

# Part 06 — Home Manager & Workstation Portability

### Ch 06.1 — Home Manager Architecture Choices
- Standalone installation (`home-manager switch`) vs. Integrated NixOS Module (`home-manager.nixosModules.home-manager`).
- Multi-OS portability: Reusing dotfile configurations on Linux and macOS (`nix-darwin`).

### Ch 06.2 — Declarative Dotfiles & Shell Tooling
- Managing dotfiles via `home.file` and `xdg.configFile`.
- Configuring daily CLI tools declaratively: `programs.git`, `programs.zsh`, `programs.tmux`, `programs.neovim`, `programs.ghostty`.
- User systemd units and environment variable export.

# Part 07 — Production Packaging: Derivations, `stdenv` & Cross-Compilation

### Ch 07.1 — `stdenv.mkDerivation` Architecture
- Derivation phase lifecycle: `unpackPhase` $\rightarrow$ `patchPhase` $\rightarrow$ `configurePhase` $\rightarrow$ `buildPhase` $\rightarrow$ `checkPhase` $\rightarrow$ `installPhase` $\rightarrow$ `fixupPhase`.
- Dependency classifications:
  - `nativeBuildInputs`: Tools executed on build host (compilers, autotools, pkg-config).
  - `buildInputs`: Libraries linked for target host (openssl, zlib).
  - `propagatedBuildInputs`: Dependencies passed down to downstream package consumers.
- Source fetchers: `fetchurl`, `fetchFromGitHub`, `fetchgit`, `fetchpatch`, and prefetching workflows (`nix-prefetch-git`, `nix-hash`).

### Ch 07.2 — Polyglot Language Packaging
- **Go:** `buildGoModule` / vendor hashes.
- **Rust:** `buildRustPackage` / cargoHashes; crane framework awareness.
- **Python:** `buildPythonPackage` / `python.withPackages` / poetry2nix / uv.
- **Node.js:** `buildNpmPackage` / pnpm / yarn.
- **C/C++ & Binaries:** `patchelf`, RPATH modification, `wrapProgram`, `patchShebangs`.

### Ch 07.3 — Cross-Compilation & Multi-Arch Strategies
- Understanding `buildPlatform`, `hostPlatform`, and `targetPlatform`.
- Native cross-compilation with `pkgs.pkgsCross.<target>`.
- Emulated builds using `boot.binfmt.emulatedSystems` under QEMU.

### Ch 07.4 — Build Debugging & Quality Control
- Debugging failed builds: `nix log`, `nix build --keep-failed`, dropping into build sandboxes via `nix develop`.
- Package quality: Meta attributes (`meta.description`, `meta.license`, `meta.platforms`, `meta.maintainers`).

# Part 08 — Advanced Module System, Storage (Disko/Impermanence) & Secrets

### Ch 08.1 — Authoring Custom NixOS Modules
- Module structure: `options` (declarative schema) and `config` (implementation).
- Types library: `types.bool`, `types.str`, `types.int`, `types.listOf`, `types.submodule`, `types.enum`, `types.attrsOf`.
- Priority resolution: Resolving option collisions with `mkIf`, `mkDefault`, `mkForce`, and `mkMerge`.
- User validation: Adding custom static assertions (`assertions`) and warnings (`warnings`).

### Ch 08.2 — Storage Mechanics: Disko & Impermanence
- **Declarative Disk Partitioning (`disko`):** Formatting GPT, LUKS encryption, Btrfs subvolumes, and ZFS pools purely from Nix code.
- **Impermanence Architecture (`tmpfs-as-root`):**
  - Running `/` on ephemeral RAM (`tmpfs`) or auto-rolling back Btrfs/ZFS root subvolumes on boot.
  - Auditing state boundaries: isolating persistent data (`/persist/var/lib`, `/persist/etc/ssh`) from ephemeral operating system noise.

### Ch 08.3 — Secrets Management Architecture
- **Threat Model:** Why plaintext secrets in store paths are world-readable and unacceptable for production.
- **`sops-nix`:** SOPS + Age/PGP encryption; decrypting secrets directly to RAM (`/run/secrets/`, `tmpfs`).
- **`agenix`:** SSH-host-key-based age encryption.
- **Systemd Credentials (`systemd-creds`):** Leveraging `LoadCredential=` and `SetCredential=` to pass encrypted secrets to services without file system store paths.
- **Hardware-Backed FDE:** Auto-unlocking LUKS disks via TPM2 (`systemd-cryptenroll`) and YubiKey under systemd stage 1.

# Part 09 — Distributed Infrastructure: Remote Provisioning, Fleet Deploy & VM Testing

### Ch 09.1 — Zero-Touch Bare-Metal & Cloud Provisioning
- **`nixos-anywhere`:** Kexec-based remote NixOS installation over SSH onto running non-NixOS Linux hosts.
- Combining `disko` + `nixos-anywhere` + `flakes` for automated from-scratch server bootstrapping.

### Ch 09.2 — Multi-Host Fleet Management
- Remote deployment tools comparison:

| Tool | Architecture | Key Capabilities |
|------|--------------|------------------|
| `nixos-rebuild --target-host` | Sequential SSH | Basic remote rebuild |
| **Colmena** | Parallel / Tag-based | High-performance fleet deployment, server tags, selective apply |
| **deploy-rs** | Flake-native | Atomic rollbacks on activation failure, multi-profile support |

- GitOps control plane patterns: Continuous deployment from git branches to target nodes.

### Ch 09.3 — NixOS Integration VM Testing (`nixosTest`)
- Headless QEMU VM testing harness (`nixpkgs.testers.runNixOSTest`).
- Authoring Python-based integration test scripts to verify multi-node networks, service startup, and firewall rules in `nix flake check`.

# Part 10 — Enterprise CI/CD, Binary Cache Build Farms & OCI Containers

### Ch 10.1 — Binary Cache Architecture & Substituters
- Public cache mechanics (`cache.nixos.org`), cryptographic signing keys, and substituter trust models (`trusted-public-keys`).
- **Self-Hosted Caches:** Operating private binary cache build farms using **Attic** or **Harmonia** (S3 backend support, GC pruning).
- Hosted cache service: **Cachix** integration.

### Ch 10.2 — CI/CD Pipeline Automation
- Building Nix matrix pipelines (GitHub Actions, Woodpecker CI, Gitea Actions).
- Optimizing CI build speeds: Cache restoration, remote build workers (`nix.buildMachines`), and offloading architecture builds.

### Ch 10.3 — OCI Container & Cloud Image Generation
- Reproducible container builds without Dockerfiles (`pkgs.dockerTools.buildLayeredImage`).
- Ad-hoc container creation via **Nixery**.
- Generating VM images (AWS AMI, Proxmox LXC/VM, QCOW2, ISO) using **`nixos-generators`**.

# Part 11 — Production Hardening, Compliance & Disaster Recovery

### Ch 11.1 — Systemd Service Hardening & Isolation
- Service sandboxing options: `DynamicUser=true`, `ProtectSystem="strict"`, `ProtectHome=true`, `PrivateTmp=true`, `NoNewPrivileges=true`, `CapabilityBoundingSet=`.
- Kernel hardening options (`security.*`) and AppArmor profiles.

### Ch 11.2 — Supply Chain Security & SBOM Compliance
- Generating Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for Nix flakes.
- Auditing unfree packages (`allowUnfreePredicate`) and vulnerability scanning (`vulnix`).

### Ch 11.3 — Production Incident Response & Disaster Recovery
- Formulating Disaster Recovery (DR) runbooks: Differentiating Nix configuration code from persistent database state.
- Simulating disaster recovery: Restoring a complete node failure from scratch in $<15\text{ minutes}$ using `nixos-anywhere` and backups.

### Ch 12.1 — Under the Hood: Evaluator & Store Mechanics
- Reading raw `.drv` files and AST graph visualizations.
- **Content-Addressed (CA) Derivations:** Early-cutoff build optimizations and content-hash caching.
- **Evaluator Profiling:** Diagnosing slow Nix evaluation using `nix eval --show-trace`, flamegraphs, and memory profiling.

### Ch 12.2 — Ecosystem Evolution & Upstream Contribution
- Upgrades strategy: Upgrading production nodes across release lines (25.11 $\rightarrow$ 26.05 $\rightarrow$ 26.11).

# Part 99 — Appendices & Production Capstone

### Appendix A — Canonical Resource Reference Matrix
- Manuals: NixOS Manual, Nixpkgs Manual, Nix Reference Manual, nix.dev.
- Community books: *NixOS & Flakes Book* (thiscute.world), *Zero to Nix*, *Nix Pills*.

### Appendix B — 26.05 Operator Command Cheatsheet

```bash
# Evaluate and build system closure
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.server01.config.system.build.toplevel

# Deploy fleet in parallel using Colmena
colmena apply --on @production

# Run headless NixOS integration tests
nix flake check --show-trace

# Inspect GC roots locking disk space
nix-store --query --roots

# Remotely provision bare-metal server from scratch
nixos-anywhere --flake .#server01 root@192.168.1.50
```

### Appendix C — Production Milestone Capstone Blueprint
Construct a complete self-hosted production infrastructure containing:
1. Modular Flake repository structured with `flake-parts`.
2. Multi-node cluster provisioned via `disko` + `nixos-anywhere`.
3. Secret encryption via `sops-nix` and `systemd-creds`.
4. Automated CI pipeline building closures and pushing to a self-hosted Attic binary cache.
5. Headless multi-node VM tests (`nixosTest`) asserting network policy and service health.
